title: Astro Portal API v1 uploads and captures
description: The initial, non-resumable upload of an already processed image, and the private "My Captures" listing it feeds. Content-addressed and therefore idempotent: the same bytes uploaded twice yield one capture, never a second row for the same tenant. A capture is private to its tenant until its owner makes it public (`visibility`); this contract carries no public URL and no slug. Its owner reads the state of its two checks (`checks`), never the machine reason of the automatic one. A capture belongs to at most one session, but may show several targets when one processed image covers more than one (a wide field, a mosaic pane): `targetIds` is the list, deduplicated idempotently as later uploads of the same bytes add targets rather than creating a second row. A resumable transport (api/uploads.md) takes over from it; the capture resource is meant to survive that. See api/v1.md, section "Uploads and captures".

sha256.description: Lowercase hex digest of the stored bytes, unprefixed. The server always recomputes it; a declared value that disagrees is a refusal, never a stored claim.

targetIds.description: Every target this capture shows, in the order given, deduplicated. 0 items is a still-unclassified draft; the cap of 16 matches a mosaic pane's realistic span, not a plan's target list.

uploadMetadata.description: The `metadata` part of the multipart POST /v1/uploads body, AND (`api/uploads.md`) the JSON body of the resumable protocol's create step, `POST /v1/uploads` with an `application/json` Content-Type instead — the two share this one shape on purpose, a create request IS an upload's declared metadata. On the multipart form it MUST precede the `file` part so the server can refuse an oversized or unentitled upload before reading any bytes; the resumable form never carries file bytes on this call at all. `targetId` is a tolerated single-item alias for `targetIds`, kept for callers written before the multi-target decision; a request carrying both is the union of the two, deduplicated. Exceeding 16 distinct targets (directly, via the alias, or once unioned onto an existing capture on replay) is `400` `invalid_request` and writes nothing. `captureId` names an existing capture of the space these bytes add an image to (a variant, not main, private; `404 capture_not_found` for another space's or an unknown one; `409 capture_variant_limit_reached` past `capture.variant_limit`); `source` is the image's source from a device (`phone`, `astro-sync`, `stacking`; a device never declares `web`, and the web session's images are always `web`; absent: `astro-sync` for Astro Sync, `phone` otherwise). Bytes the space already holds, as any image of any capture, store nothing and are never refused for a limit.

role.description: `progression` declares a progression image of `captureId` (required with it): a milestone of the night Astro Sync stacked, the history of that capture — never its main image, never a variant, not counted against `capture.variant_limit` (only against the storage), shown on the capture's page and with the capture in its galleries. `plan` declares the image of a multi-night plan (`projectId` required, `captureId`, `sessionId` and `planId` absent): a new capture of the space attached to that plan, in no night's captures and no variant of one; it needs the multi-night plans of Astro Sync (`analysis.progression`), else `403 multi_night_not_active`.

projectId.description: The multi-night plan an image of role `plan` belongs to; only with that role (`404 project_not_found` for another space's or an unknown one).

combinedNightIds.description: The nights (`sessionId`) whose integrations the image of the plan combines; only with role `plan`.

totalsByFilter.description: The image of the plan's total by filter (`integration.schema.json`, `planTotal`); only with role `plan`.

planRender.description: The render of the image of the plan (`natural`, `dualband`, `polished`, `hoo`, `none`); only with role `plan`.

progressionFrames.description: The light frames the milestone stacks; only with `role` `progression`.

stage.description: The stage the web session asks for its new capture, `draft` or `finalized` (the default). A device's upload is always a draft, whatever it declares.

metadataSource.description: The producer the proposals below come from — `astro-sync` or `import`. Absent: `astro-sync` for Astro Sync's token or an image of Astro Sync (`source` `astro-sync`, `stacking`); a phone's upload proposing without it is refused (`400 invalid_metadata`), and the web session proposes nothing at an upload (its owner writes on the detail).

title.description: A proposal of the capture's title (80 characters at most). Every proposal is optional, applied under `metadataSource`, never over a value the owner edited, and listed in the answer's `skipped` when left.

description.description: A proposal of the capture's description (2 000 characters at most; the import joins its technical text after a blank line).

acquisition.description: Proposed acquisition lines, one per filter and exposure (40 at most). A line is matched by its filter and its exposure: a line proposed earlier and untouched is updated, a missing one added, a line the owner corrected or deleted left (`skipped`).

calibration.description: A proposal of the calibration, free text of 120 characters at most (a longer one is refused, never shortened).

processing.description: A proposal of the processing: `software` (120 characters at most), `steps` (500 at most).

variantTitle.description: A proposal of the owner's `title` of the image sent, in one language (90 characters at most): the import's menu label, the owner's own words of the old portal. Titles need not be unique within a capture. Never over an image whose texts the owner wrote. Astro Sync sends `variantGeneratedTitle` instead.

variantDescription.description: A proposal of the owner's `description` of the image sent, in one language (280 characters at most). Astro Sync sends `variantGeneratedDescription` instead.

variantGeneratedTitle.description: Additive: the title the producer generated for the image sent, in the ten languages, English required (capture-variant.schema.json `generatedTitle`): Astro Sync's name of the processing and its settings. Stored apart from the owner's title, whatever he wrote.

variantGeneratedDescription.description: Additive: the description the producer generated for the image sent, in the ten languages, English required (capture-variant.schema.json `generatedDescription`).

variantProcessing.description: Additive: what made the image sent (`software` 120 characters at most, `steps` 500 at most), the image's own, kept with it (`null` or absent proposes nothing). The capture shows the steps of its main image: this image's become the capture's while it is the main one, and again when the owner picks it as such, never over what he wrote. A variant sent with `processing` leaves the capture's untouched; with `variantProcessing` it keeps its own.

imageQuality.description: Additive: the quality of the image sent, measured by the producer on the stacked master before any stretch (`imageQuality`). A producer's proposal only: sent by the phone or by the web session it is `400 invalid_metadata` (`field: imageQuality`). Kept under the capability `analysis.logs`: without it the service drops the field, stores the image all the same and lists `{ field: "imageQuality", reason: "capability" }` in `skipped`; a private server keeps it. Read back as `quality` of the image (capture-variant.schema.json) and, for the main image, of the owner's resource.

Additive: the quality of a stacked image, as Astro Sync measured it when it sent it — the stars of the image itself, not the medians of the night (`detail.sessionQuality` of the owner's resource is that). `measuredOn` says on what: `linear`, the master before any stretch (an image processed elsewhere, stretched or deconvolved, has no quality: its FWHM would compare with nothing). `fwhmPixels` is the median full width at half maximum of the stars in pixels; `fwhmArcsec` the same in arcseconds, `null` when the pixel scale is not known; `eccentricity` between 0 and 1 (`null` when not measured); `starCount` the stars measured; `measuredAt` when; `tool` the program and its version. Written by a producer, read by anyone who reads the capture, never held by a right.

acquisitionSummary.description: Additive: items of `GET /v1/captures` only: what a card says of the capture's lines of « Intégrations » without a second call — « Intégration 4 h » (`integrationSeconds`), « 40 × 180 s » (`frameCount`, `exposureSeconds`). `exposureSeconds` is the exposure every line shares, `null` when the lines differ; `frameCount` and `integrationSeconds` add up the lines (a declared line whose poses are not known counts its declared time and no frame). The whole summary is `null` for a capture with no line.

proposedAcquisitionLine.description: One acquisition line a producer proposes: `filter` (free text, 40 characters at most, never normalised; `null` for none), `frameCount` (≥ 1), `exposureSeconds` (> 0), `gain` (an integer or `null`). The integration is computed by the service, never sent.

computerLabel.description: Additive: the computer the producer (Astro Sync) measured the line on, as it names it (80 characters at most); `null` or absent when it did not say. Read back as `computerLabel` of the line.

skipped.description: What a producer's proposals left — `{ field, reason }`, `reason` `edited` (the owner's value, never overwritten) or `deleted` (an acquisition line the owner deleted); `capability`, additive (a proposal the space has no right to keep — `imageQuality` without `analysis.logs`; the rest of the request is applied). Absent or empty when everything proposed was applied or already there.

captureTag.description: One of the owner's own tags of a capture (`capture_tags.tag`), free text exactly as typed (trimmed, never otherwise normalised), 40 characters at most.

captureTags.description: The owner's own tags of a capture, read in the order of their text, 20 at most. Shown in the private gallery only, never in the public gallery.

visibility.description: `private` (the default of every capture): seen in its own space and its private gallery only. `public`: also in the public gallery, as long as it is not removed from it nor refused on review.

checks.description: The two checks of a capture as its owner reads them. `automatic`: the automatic check, `null` until it has run, then `sky` (recognised as the sky or a landscape), `undetermined` (a person, or neither a sky nor a landscape: an administrator looks before any publication) or `other` (the check did not pass); its machine reason is never sent, but for the reasons of `automaticReason`. `team`: the verification flag, `null` until an administrator looks, then `approved` or `refused`, with its reason when refused. `reviewRequestedAt`: when the owner asked for a verification. `protectionNoticeAt` and `protectionLiftedAt`: the notice of a private capture that did not pass, and when its private protection was lifted. `removedFromGalleryAt`: when reports removed it from the public gallery, `null` again once it is approved.

automaticReason.description: Additive. Present only when `automatic` is `undetermined`: why the service could not read the file — `check_off` (the check is switched off on this server), `unreadable`, `too_large`, `too_slow`, `unsupported_format` (a format the check does not read) or `raw_camera_file` (a camera's raw file) —, or why an administrator looks before any publication: `person_detected` (a person seems to be in the image) or `not_recognised` (neither a sky nor a landscape was recognised with enough confidence). The last four are additive; a client that does not know one shows the result without a reason. Never the figure of the rule that fell short (too few stars, a calibration frame, an astronomical header without coordinates…), which stays with the administration, and never sent for any other result.

capture.description: `originalName` is echoed exactly as the person named the file and is never used as a filesystem path. `status` is `uploaded` for a complete single-request upload; `draft` is reserved for the resumable protocol (`api/uploads.md`). `targetIds` is always the full, current list — the resource never carries a singular `targetId`; a client that still reads the alias should read `targetIds[0]`. `visibility` is `private` or `public`; `checks` is the state of its two checks, for its owner. `protectionLiftsAt` is on the items of `GET /v1/captures` only; `tags` (the owner's own tags) on those items too, read only. `stage` is `draft` or `finalized`, distinct from the visibility (an upload from a device is a draft, private; the web's is finalized, private; a draft is never public nor in a gallery); `sha256`, `byteSize` and `originalName` are the capture's main image's. The items of `GET /v1/captures` also carry what a device's gallery draws without a second call: `visibilityEditable`, `thumbnail`, `galleryLabel`, `nightDate`, `width`, `height`, `targets`, `mainImageId` and `imageCount`. Journal (additive): a capture is linked to its session by `sessionId` (set at the upload, or by the service when the upload names none but a target and a night: the session of that `eveningDate` that carries the target; `PATCH /v1/manage/captures/{id}` can set it to another session or to `null`); `GET /v1/captures?sessionId=` lists a session's captures; there is **one capture per session and target**, a second image for it replaces the image or becomes a variant (`replaced`, `replacedAt`, `replacedSource`). `nightDate` keeps its own definition, distinct from a session's `eveningDate`.

stage.description: `draft` (« Brouillon ») or `finalized` (« Finalisée »). Written by the service on every answer; optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates.

madePublicAt.description: Additive: the instant the capture last turned public (« Publique depuis le … »). Written by the service as the capture goes from private to public, cleared as it goes private again, left alone by a write that keeps it public. Only on a public capture (absent while it is private); `null` for a capture that was already public when the date began to be kept: the date is unknown, never guessed. Optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates; a reader shows « date inconnue » (never a made-up date) for a public capture without a date.

archivedAt.description: Additive: present only on a capture archived after the end of a subscription: when it was archived. The owner still reads and exports it, « Mes captures » labels it « Archivée », no gallery shows it; a resubscription removes the field. A reader of an earlier answer, and a capture that is not archived, has no such field.

protectionLiftsAt.description: On the items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the date the private protection of a capture that did not pass the automatic check is (or was) lifted, the notice's date plus `ASTRO_PORTAL_CHECK_NOTICE_DAYS`, computed by the service (« sera levée le 20 octobre »); `null` when no notice runs.

tags.description: On the items of `GET /v1/captures` (and the owner's routes of the web): the owner's own tags of the capture. The phone reads them and writes them too (`PATCH /v1/captures/{id}` `{ tags }`, the whole list); the web enters them in « Mon espace » → « Captures ». Optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates; the answer of an upload never carries it.

revision.description: Additive: the capture's revision, an integer that is 1 at the creation and moves by 1 at each write of the capture — a metadata field, the tags, the stage, the visibility, the session, an image added, replaced or removed, a producer's proposal that changed something, a synchronisation of the lines; a write that leaves the stored value as it was moves nothing. The web and the phone write the same capture: each owner write names the revision it read (`If-Match: "<revision>"`) and the service refuses it with `409 capture_conflict` only if the field it writes changed after that revision (v1.md, « A capture written by two hands »). On the owner's resource and on each item of both lists; written by the service on every answer, optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates.

title.description: Additive: items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the capture's own title — the owner's, else a producer's proposal (80 characters at most); `null` when it has none, the screen then names the capture by its targets. The owner's resource carries it with its origin in `metadata.title`.

acquisitionSummary.description: Additive: items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the summary of the capture's lines of « Intégrations » (`acquisitionSummary`); `null` when it has no line.

visibilityEditable.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: whether this caller may change the visibility — never a device (the visibility is the web's), the web session for a finalized or public capture.

thumbnail.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: whether the main image has its thumbnail (`GET /v1/captures/{id}/media?variant=thumbnail`).

galleryLabel.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the generic label of the public gallery — the first target's (its type for a catalogue target, its chosen label for a personal one), « Grand champ » without a target, `null` for a type without one.

nightDate.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the night of its plan, else of its session, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

width.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the main image's pixels, once read.

targets.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the targets of `targetIds`, resolved in their order — a catalogue target with its designation, type, aliases and position (hours, degrees), a personal target of the space with its name and label.

mainImageId.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: the id of the main image (capture-variant.schema.json).

imageCount.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: how many images the capture holds, its main image included.

mainImageSource.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: where the main image came from (`phone`, `web`, `astro-sync`, `stacking`; `null` when never recorded). Astro Sync's « Annotations » says « Envoyée depuis le téléphone » and fetches its original (`GET /v1/captures/{id}/original`).

replacedAt.description: Additive: when the capture's image was last **replaced** by another one for the same session and target (a space without the right to variants, `capture.variant_limit` = 0, keeps one image per capture: the new one takes the place of the old, the old bytes released from the quota). `null` while it never was. The screens say it (« Astro Sync a remplacé la photo envoyée du téléphone par son image. »). Written by the service; optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates.

replacedSource.description: Additive: the `source` of the image that was replaced (`phone` for the photo sent from the phone, the usual case); the source of the new image is `mainImageSource`. `null` while `replacedAt` is. With `replacedAt`, the most recent replacement only.

replacedMadePrivate.description: Additive, present and `true` only: the replacement of the capture's image turned a **public** capture back to **private** (the new image has passed no check; a public capture must be validated again explicitly). It stays `true` until the owner next writes the visibility (publishes it again, or chooses private); absent otherwise, and a reader reads absent as `false`. The screens say so at the replacement (« Votre capture est redevenue privée, car son image a été remplacée. ») and on the capture afterwards, which an Astro Sync replacement leaves unseen.

skySolved.description: Items of `GET /v1/captures` only: whether the main image has its sky solution (`sky-solution.schema.json`); `?skySolution=missing` lists the captures where it is `false`, whatever device or page sent them.

projectId.description: Only on the image of a multi-night plan (role `plan`): the plan it belongs to. Absent on every other capture.

plan.description: With `projectId`: the nights it combines, its totals by filter and its render (`integration.schema.json`, `planCapture`).

storage.description: The tenant's own storage position, mirroring the capability values so a client can show a bar without a second call. `quotaBytes` and `maxFileBytes` are zero when media storage is not part of the current profile — zero means none, not unlimited. `captureCount` is how many captures the space holds, the uploads in progress included in an upload answer and its refusal, and `captureCountLimit` is the value of `capture.count_limit` (`0` no allowance, the unlimited sentinel no cap): « 2 captures sur 3 » and the number in the refusal come from them, never from a constant. The service always writes the two; they stay optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates. `usedBytes` counts every stored image of every capture.

variantLimit.description: `Capture.variant_limit`, the variants a capture may hold besides its main image (`0`: the main image only; the unlimited sentinel: no cap).

variantCount.description: In the answer and the refusal of an upload that adds a variant to a capture, how many variants it holds besides its main image.

uploadResponse.description: `201` on the first upload of these bytes, `200` with `deduplicated: true` on any later one. A replay returns the existing capture, never a second row, and never re-associates it with another session or plan. It MAY grow `capture.targetIds`: a replay's targets are unioned onto the existing list idempotently, and `targetsAdded` (present whenever `deduplicated` is true) counts how many were new — 0 when the replay named the same targets or none.

replaced.description: Additive: true when this upload's image **replaced** the image of the capture it belongs to (one capture per session and target; a space without the right to variants), false when it was added as a variant, as the main image with the former one kept as a variant, or created a capture. Absent on an answer written before the lot; a reader assumes false.

variant.description: The variant an upload with `captureId` added (or the image found already there).

list.description: GET /v1/captures (additive). The private My Captures view: the person's own captures with the observation session, plan and targets each one belongs to. By default the synchronisation's reading: oldest first by the later of `createdAt` and the instant the capture came back from the trash of its session (`createdAt` itself is the date it was added and never moves), walked by `?since=` and `nextSince` (that instant, for the last row). With `?order=recent` (Journal F, additive) the most recent first -- by the night of the capture, then by the moment it was added -- walked by `?before=` and `nextBefore` (`nextSince` is then `null`); `order=recent` and `since` are not asked together. An optional `?targetId=` query filters to captures whose `targetIds` contains it, and (additive) `?sessionId=` to the captures of one session (the session's id; a capture belongs to at most one); the two add up. The schema does not model query parameters, only this response shape.

nextBefore.description: Journal F (additive), only with `?order=recent`: the opaque cursor to send back as `?before=` for the next page, `null` on the last. Absent on the synchronisation's reading; a reader assumes null.

publishingBlocked.description: Whether the person is blocked from making a capture public (the block on publishing, `publishing_blocked`, a state of the person, not the capability `capture.public`). Uploading is never refused for it. The phone shows it and never asks to make a capture public. Written by the service; optional so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates.

refusal.description: The capability refusal body. It repeats the deciding numbers so an interface can explain the refusal without a second call, and names no product or offer. `capture_variant_limit_reached` (409) refuses an image added to a capture past `capture.variant_limit`, with `storage.variantLimit` and `storage.variantCount`.

limit.description: With `invalid_metadata`, the field's limit (characters, or the bound), `null` when it has none.

uploadSession.description: The resumable protocol (`api/uploads.md`): the shared envelope `POST /v1/uploads` (JSON create), `PUT /v1/uploads/{id}` and `GET /v1/uploads/{id}` all answer. `offset` is always the server's own durable count — after a `PUT` it is what was actually written, never an echo of what the client asked to write. `expiresAt` is `null` once `completed` is true: a completed session is not subject to the 72-hour expiry. `captureId` appears only once `completed` is true.

present.description: `true` when the create step found these bytes already held by the space (any image of any capture) and answered before any chunk — `completed` is then `true` with that `captureId` and `imageId`.

uploadFinalizeResponse.description: `POST /v1/uploads/{id}/finalize` on success: `uploadSession`'s own fields (always `completed: true`, always a `captureId`) plus the created-or-deduplicated capture, exactly like the non-resumable `uploadResponse`. Idempotent — calling finalize again after success replays this same body.

replaced.description: Additive: true when this upload's image **replaced** the image of the capture it belongs to (one capture per session and target; a space without the right to variants), false when it was added as a variant, as the main image with the former one kept as a variant, or created a capture. Absent on an answer written before the lot; a reader assumes false.

variant.description: The variant an upload with `captureId` added (or the image found already there).

uploadRefusal.description: The resumable protocol's own structured refusals (`api/uploads.md`): a wrong `PUT` offset, a finalize whose bytes have not all arrived yet, a finalize whose assembled digest disagrees with what was declared at creation, or a finalize whose capture (`captureId` at creation) has left the space since (`upload_capture_gone`: create again, the bytes are kept). `offset` repeats the server's own current, durable offset — `0` after a hash mismatch resets the session for a full re-upload — so a client can resume without a second `GET`. Distinct from `refusal` above, which is the capability/quota refusal shape.
